# A rail reveal enters with an 8px nudge, not a slide from its own edge

Sub-issue of #13158 (dock layouts). The second of the dock-polish leaves the demo plan named (L2 — reveal motion); siblings: #18070 (L3, the reveal's geometry on a padded host), #18071 (L4, header-action tooltips).

## Context

Clicking a rail tab reveals the auto-hidden pane as an overlay next to the strip. Today the overlay *appears*: it fades from 40% opacity and moves 8px, over the shared dock duration. The operator's design read (2026-09-02, the demo rehearsal): a reveal should **slide in from the edge that owns it** — a right rail slides right-to-left while the overlay's opacity rises, in the order of 300ms — so the eye reads where the pane came from and where it will go back to.

## The Problem

The motion exists but is a nudge, not a slide. Measured on `dev@5ae9358063`:

- `resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss:150-170` — `.neo-dashboard-dock-reveal-overlay { animation: neo-dock-reveal-fade var(--dock-transition-duration) var(--dock-transition-easing) }` with the per-edge names the rail stamps (`-left/-right/-top/-bottom`); the keyframes start at `opacity: 0.4` and `translateX(±8px)` / `translateY(±8px)`.
- `Container.scss:14/20` — `--dock-transition-duration: var(--motion-panel, 280ms)`, `--dock-transition-duration-fast: var(--motion-fast, 120ms)`; `:136-140` collapses both to `0ms` under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (the token layer owns reduced motion, per #14779).
- `src/dashboard/dock/interaction/RevealOverlay.mjs:192-214` — the overlay listens to its own `animationend`, holding one `MotionSignal.enter/leave` entry while the reveal animates (`revealMotionActive`); teardown settles the producer without an end event (`:234`).
- The hidden state is `display: none` (`Container.scss:472-474`): there is no exit motion, and none is asked for here.

An 8px travel from 40% opacity over 280ms reads as a flicker at pane scale (the overlay is 12rem+ wide); the pane's origin is not legible.

## The Architectural Reality

- #14779 established the dock motion contract: durations come from ONE token set (`--dock-transition-*`), never literals at call sites; motion is observable (`dock-animating` / `animationend`-driven completion); reduced motion collapses at the token layer. The reveal already rides that contract through the overlay's `animationend` → `MotionSignal` pair — a longer or different keyframe keeps it as long as the animation still ends on the overlay element.
- The per-edge cls (`neo-dashboard-dock-reveal-overlay-<edge>`) is stamped by the rail (`RevealOverlay.mjs:291-294`), so the direction is already known to CSS; the change is confined to keyframes and one token.
- ADR 0029 §2.6 (auto-hide interaction layer, #13280): the reveal is runtime-only geometry; motion does not touch the document.
- Not this leaf: where the overlay starts (touching the strip vs. covering it) is #18070's geometry; a reveal inside an iframe pane is #18067.

## The Fix

`resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss`:

1. One new token in the existing set: `--dock-transition-duration-reveal: var(--motion-reveal, 300ms)`, collapsed to `0ms` in the reduced-motion block beside its siblings.
2. The overlay's `animation` reads that token (easing stays `--dock-transition-easing`, the soft ease-out).
3. The four per-edge keyframes start **fully outside the overlay's own box** and transparent: `from { opacity: 0; transform: translateX(100%) }` for `-right` (`-100%` for `-left`, `translateY(±100%)` for `-bottom` / `-top`); the edge-less fallback keeps a fade from 0.
4. `overflow` on the reveal's host must clip the travel so the overlay never paints over the strip mid-flight — read the host rule before adding one; if the rail host already clips, no change.

No JavaScript changes are expected; if `MotionSignal` needs the animation name (it should not — it listens to `animationend` on the overlay), that is a finding to record, not to work around.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dock-transition-duration-reveal` (new token, `Container.scss` token block) | #14779 (one token set, no literals) | 300ms via `var(--motion-reveal, 300ms)`; `0ms` under reduced motion | absent token → the `var()` default | ADR 0029 §2.6 one line | component arm reads `animation-duration` |
| `@keyframes neo-dock-reveal-from-{left,right,top,bottom}` (`Container.scss:167-170`) | this ticket | start at `opacity: 0`, `translate*(±100%)` | — | same line | component arm samples the transform at t≈0 and settled |
| `.neo-dashboard-dock-reveal-overlay` `animation` (`Container.scss:153`) | #14779 | duration from the new token | — | — | same arm |
| `RevealOverlay` `animationend` → `MotionSignal` (`RevealOverlay.mjs:192-214`) | #14779 / #14929 | unchanged; must still settle after the longer animation | — | — | existing unit arm + the component arm's settle wait |

Decision Record impact: aligned-with ADR 0029 (§2.6 runtime-only reveal); amends nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After a rail-tab click in a real browser, the overlay's computed `animation-name` is the owning edge's keyframe and `animation-duration` is `0.3s`; sampled within the first frame its transform carries the edge-ward offset, settled it is the identity — a component spec under `test/playwright/component/dashboard/` on an existing dock-rail fixture, one arm per horizontal edge at least, red on `dev` (today's transform at t≈0 is ≤ 8px).
- [ ] With `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` emulated, the same read is `0s` (the token layer collapses it; no per-site check).
- [ ] The overlay still settles: `MotionSignal` leaves after the animation and the existing rail / overlay unit specs stay green (`test/playwright/unit/dashboard/`).
- [ ] Visual read on the FM cockpit and on `apps/workstation` (right rail and left rail), both themes: the pane slides in from its strip and never paints over the strip mid-flight; screenshots in the PR, design-read.
- [ ] No duration literal at the call site (review-checkable, #14779 AC).

## Out of Scope

- Exit motion (the hidden state is `display: none`; a two-phase hide is its own leaf if wanted).
- The overlay's start geometry on padded hosts (#18070), iframe dismissal (#18067), header-action tooltips (#18071).
- Pin / restore transitions (FLIP layer, #14929).
